correctness.rationale: The full Laplacian's degree diagonals survive deletion; pinning yields a positive definite principal submatrix. Simultaneous layer reversal and rung permutation exhaust the six leader-pair types. The stated inverse-block trace formula is obtained by squaring the block inverse, and the hub-pinned blocks have eigenvalues 1 and 1+2t. Independently reproduced every sign certificate via grounded characteristic determinants in /workspace/checks/book_determinants.py: compress the m-2 ordinary rungs to their constant mode, adding m-3 copies of the two-rung-block eigenvalues on the difference subspace. At m=2, the representative ordinary block is triangularly decoupled and its extra factor cancels. Use the first three determinant coefficients to obtain the inverse-square trace, rather than the frozen inverse-block formula. The shifted numerator term counts/minima are 21/1,21/1,32/1,22/4,32/4; all five are explicitly nonzero and positive at m=3 too. Denominators have positive coefficients. At m=2 the exact HH–LLd comparison, elimination of HS/LLs/LLc, both HO polynomials and the endpoint t=3/5 reproduce. Descartes and the sign bracket give a unique positive crossing at 0.622700872736214..., with only HH and the two LLd placements tied. At (3,1) the first-order HO cost 95/24 beats the hub cost 4, whereas the second-order unique hub optimum costs 10/3. The uploaded checker was inspected, not run; the all-parameter evidence is symbolic, not finite sampling.

value.rationale: Exactly two pins and common rung weight define a natural one-parameter symmetry-preserving comparison. The persistent hub-pair optimum on every larger book and the exact exceptional two-rung tie and switch replace repeated optimization over vertex pairs. The verified reversal from the first-order three-rung objective shows concretely why solving a different coherence order is worthwhile.
